model_version: pic2d v1.1 (all-GPU step, device block-Thomas Poisson, ion subcycling, electrode-work ledger)

operating_point.neutral_density_justification: v1.1 budget: at n_g = 1e20 the 0-D particle balance n_g K_iz(T_e) V = v_B(T_e) A_loss closes at T_e ~ 8 eV (v1 ran at 5e20 where it closes at ~4 eV and the avalanche gain per injected electron was 12); static uniform background, ~0.015 mg/s equivalent effusion through the 2 mm bore at 300 K
operating_point.electron_injection_justification: power balance I_d U_a = n_eq v_B A_loss e (eps_c + 7 T_e) with I_d ~ 2-3 x I_inj gives n_eq ~ 2e17 m^-3; the resolvability budget below is written for a 2x peak-to-mean factor (n_max = 4e17)

numerics.dt_justification: a first v2 attempt at dt = 3 ps (omega_pe dt = 0.107 at the design ceiling) was stopped fail-closed by the runtime gate after 0.27 us in both coarse cases: the instantaneous peak-node density (axis nodes hold a handful of macro-particles) reached 1.4e18 m^-3 while the window-averaged peak was 4.7-5.4e17 m^-3, i.e. the gate sees ~3x shot noise on top of the physical peak; dt = 1.5 ps keeps omega_pe dt <= 0.2 up to a node density of 5.6e18 m^-3 (14x the design ceiling) so the gate only trips on a genuine runaway
numerics.ion_subcycle_justification: k dt = 12 ps; ion plasma period at n_max = 4e17 is 2 pi / omega_pi = 0.09 us, ion cyclotron period at 0.29 T is 29 us, a 21 km/s ion (full 300 V) moves 0.25 um per ion step (< 1 % of a fine cell); insensitivity k vs 2k is a unit test
numerics.poisson: device block-Thomas direct (exact to round-off, true-residual contract 1e-10 |rhs| verified at every host sync)
numerics.coarse_debye_ratio_note: the coarse pair is the under-resolved member of the convergence pair by design (dz = 100 um vs lambda_D,min = 33.2 um, ratio 3.008); its a-priori gate allows a 3.1x cell/Debye ratio and this is stated on the dashboard
numerics.averaging_window_note: consecutive 120000-step (180 ns) windows; the reported maps are the last completed window (or the current one if at least half full)

budget_v1_1.ion_transit_note: Bohm-speed radial transit 2 mm / 2.4 km/s ~ 0.8 us and a 300 V ion crossing 18 mm in 0.9 us: one transit time is taken as 1.0 us = 666667 steps

stopping_rule.description: a case runs at least min_steps (one ion transit time); after that it stops as soon as the plateau criterion holds, else at target_steps (1.6 us) or at its wall-clock budget; the reason is recorded
stopping_rule.plateau: relative drift < 5 % over the trailing 20 % of the run for both the discharge current and the plasma electron count (linear fit over the trailing window, drift = slope x window / mean)

simplifications: static uniform neutral background (no depletion, no neutral flow) - depletion was not added in v1.1
no ion-neutral collisions (elastic or charge exchange) - not added in v1.1
electron-neutral: isotropic elastic without the 2 m_e/M energy loss, one lumped 8.32 eV excitation, single ionisation with Vahedi-Surendra secondary energy and isotropic emission
dielectric wall: perfectly absorbing with accumulated surface charge, zero field in the dielectric backing (perfect insulator), no secondary electron emission, no sputtering
exit plane: Dirichlet 0 V cathode/neutraliser reference; electrons injected there as a flux-weighted half-Maxwellian at fixed current
anode: perfectly absorbing conductor at fixed potential
cone wall represented as a one-cell stair-step of the plasma cell mask
prescribed static B from the P2 solution (no plasma-induced field); bilinear node interpolation of the C1 bicubic psi field
ions pushed every 8 steps with 8 dt (frozen in between; births added to the ion charge immediately)
electrostatic only, azimuthally symmetric: no azimuthal instabilities/anomalous transport
momentum-conserving bilinear scheme: energy is not exactly conserved; the ledger (with electrode work) residual is reported

operating point scaled to a resolvable density: 3 mA injection at 300 V and n_g = 1e20 m^-3 (a real CFT runs at 0.1-1 A; the kinetic structure, not the absolute current, is the object of this screening run)
development/screening run: not preregistered, no experimental validation, not a performance prediction
